objective: Audit resolved frontier cells and task history for duplicate or near-duplicate work and determine whether a minimal novelty guard is sufficient.
bottleneck: Research efficiency depends on preserving negative evidence strongly enough to redirect search.
question: Does the durable history adequately prevent repeating equivalent experiments when a frontier cell is already resolved?
verified: Found concrete evidence that duplicate-work avoidance is insufficiently implemented: momentum variations (different lookbacks, horizons, cost models, cross-sectional approaches) are treated as independent frontier cells without detection of technical overlap.

The artifact similarity analysis reveals that momentum lookback 5, 3, and 10 are functionally equivalent tests under different lookback parameters; momentum horizon 20/60 and longer horizon tests examine the same underlying edge across time scales; momentum cross-sectional (lookback 63) tests a different variant of the same momentum class; cost sensitivity testing applies realistic costs to the same edge.
There is no systematic tracking or prevention of equivalent momentum research across these variants, indicating a gap in the novelty guard effectiveness.
unverified: Quantitative similarity metrics between different momentum artifacts (lookback, horizon, cost sensitivity, cross-sectional) have not been computed to establish formal equivalence classes.
uncertainty_targeted: duplicate-work prevention effectiveness in momentum research
uncertainty_reduced: assessment of whether current evidence tracking prevents equivalent momentum experiments
next: Implement a minimal novelty guard: add per-asset momentum signature hash to momentum_results.json tracking all variations (lookback/horizon/cross-sectional/cost) to enable duplicate detection while preserving legitimate methodological refinement.
